note: The main banks were taken as the three largest Czech banks by clients and assets, a choice from general knowledge (no central bank or association ranking was read in this pass): Česká spořitelna, ČSOB and Komerční banka. Komerční banka: its price list (Sazebník KB, in force from 1 May 2026; the changes from 1 November 2026 were read and don't touch the credit cards) and its card pages, read 2026-10-30. The 4U karta costs nothing to hold, the A karta 59 korunas a month to administer its credit, none in a month with more than 3,000 korunas of card payments (the student holder's 29 isn't written), and the World Elite card 550 korunas a month (free with a Top nabídka account or the Premium service, which the game doesn't hold). The 4U and A karta bear a fixed 22.90% a year and the World Elite 9.90%, each card's page says. Each page states a minimum of 3% a month plus interest and the 4U and A karta pages up to 45 days without interest. Cash from the shared ATM network (KB, MONETA, Air Bank, UniCredit) costs 1%, at least 30 korunas, on the 4U and A karta (other banks' ATMs at least 100 and a cash advance at least 350, not written), and nothing on the World Elite. The 500-koruna reminder charged on an unpaid instalment of 500 korunas or more is written as the late fee (the 500-koruna threshold isn't modelled), and the 20-koruna notice of an overdrawn limit as the over-limit fee. The optional automatic repayment (29 a month on the A karta), MojeKarta design, insurance, post and replacement charges aren't written. The Infinite card (850 a month) belongs to private banking and its rate is only in a notice that wasn't found, so it isn't written. Česká spořitelna: its price list for the Kreditní karta (in force from 29 April 2026, which is also its notice of interest rates), read 2026-10-30. It costs 50 korunas a month, none in a period with 3,000 korunas of card spending; the minimum is 3% of what's drawn, at least 200 korunas. Interest on a balance not repaid in full is 12 to 24% a year, charged as 10 korunas for each whole 500 korunas drawn (none under 500); the range is written, its top the rate and 12 its floor, the step rule not being the started-step form the game holds. A withdrawal from its own ATMs costs 50 korunas (80 and 125 at others, not written). The 300-koruna cost of delay, charged at the 10th day late, is written as the late fee (the further 900 at the 40th and 70th days aren't). The 4.5% surcharge applies only to currencies not on the card exchange list and isn't written. ČSOB's credit card pages answered with a captcha and weren't read. MONETA Money Bank, among the Czech Republic's five largest banks, was added in wave 4 as the third bank (ČSOB having answered with a captcha in wave 3; UniCredit Bank's card page refused the request, 403, and Raiffeisenbank's wasn't at its address, 404): its Kreditní karta Smart page, read 2026-10-30 (the page carries a reCAPTCHA key for its forms only and was served in full). The card costs 49 korunas a month to keep (the electronic statement nothing); the representative example's yearly rate, 22.99% (28.91% APR), is written as the rate; up to 50 days without interest, on purchases and cash withdrawals alike (grace 50). The page gives no cash, currency, minimum or late charge, so none is written; the cashback offers aren't written. No minimum payment share is published for MONETA's Kreditní karta Smart; tried: its card page, leaflet and price list (none stated) and its product conditions for revolving credit and credit cards (from 1 April 2025, read 2026-10-30), which make the minimum a percentage set in each contract plus the interest and fees, at least 200 korunas, without stating the percentage.
